steps.advance: Can release and transition comfortably after several short turns across two sessions.
steps.easier: Shorten play or choose a lower-arousal activity. Guarding or redirection needs individual support.

skills.title: Small comfortable spin
skills.goal: Turn a comfortable circle for fun.
skills.setup: Non-slip surface; skip for pain, dizziness, or mobility concerns.

steps.title: Guide a partial circle
steps.teach: At nose height, slowly guide a treat a little toward one shoulder. Reward a small turn, then return to neutral. Build a quarter circle, half circle, and a comfortable complete circle over short sessions. Keep feet on the floor and avoid tight pivots.
steps.advance: Can follow a wide comfortable circle without slipping or tension.
steps.easier: Use only a quarter turn or skip this trick if movement is uncomfortable.

steps.title: Fade the lure and add the word
steps.teach: Use the same broad circle with an empty hand and reward afterward. Say “spin” before the familiar gesture, then gradually make the gesture smaller. Teach the other direction separately if wanted, with an equally comfortable circle.
steps.advance: Turns on the chosen cue/signal without visible food on 4 of 5 attempts across two sessions.
steps.easier: Restore a larger hand signal or reward a half circle; keep repetitions brief.

skills.title: Offer a paw
skills.goal: Voluntarily place one paw onto an open hand.
skills.setup: Dog comfortable lifting a paw; no grabbing or shaking the leg.

steps.title: Capture a small paw lift
steps.teach: Offer a low open palm beside a front paw without touching it. Reward a natural weight shift or small paw lift. Over brief repetitions reward a lift toward your hand, then light voluntary contact. Do not squeeze a paw or hold food in a fist to provoke scratching.
steps.advance: Offers light paw contact on most easy presentations with comfortable balance.
steps.easier: Reward a smaller lift or practice a nose target instead if paw work is uncomfortable.

steps.title: Add the cue and a quick release
steps.teach: Say “paw” before offering the familiar palm. Mark contact and lower your hand promptly so the dog can place the foot back down. Fade extra gestures gradually and reward afterward. This trick does not imply permission to restrain the paw for care.
steps.advance: Offers the paw on a cue/signal on 4 of 5 attempts across two sessions, with a relaxed immediate release.
steps.easier: Lower your hand and shorten contact. Skip if the dog withdraws or seems uncomfortable.

skills.title: Tug a rope handle
skills.goal: Gently pull one designated handle and release.
skills.setup: Large intact rope handle, supervised; no mouth pain or guarding. Remove ropes after practice.

steps.title: Take the rope handle
steps.teach: Offer a large intact rope handle at comfortable mouth height. Use the familiar take and drop cues and reward. Mark a gentle grip; no chewing, jumping, or hard tug is needed. Use a handle that cannot catch feet or neck.
steps.advance: Willingly takes and releases this handle without chewing or tension.
steps.easier: Try a softer suitable handle and shorter grips. If teeth or neck appear uncomfortable, skip pulling.

steps.title: Reward tiny backward tension
steps.teach: Hold the handle very lightly. As the dog grips, allow a tiny backward weight shift to create almost no resistance; mark that pull and then request a release and reward. Do not yank against the dog or require a forceful neck movement.
steps.advance: Makes a small gentle pull and releases on 4 of 5 easy attempts.
steps.easier: Reward a smaller weight shift and remove all resistance.

steps.title: Transfer to a lightweight hinged prop
steps.teach: Attach the handle securely to a stable lightweight training door or board that moves very easily without swinging into the dog. Cue the familiar grip and gentle pull, then reward a tiny movement. Build only enough movement to understand cause and effect.
steps.advance: Opens the easy prop with one gentle pull and releases on 4 of 5 attempts in two sessions.
steps.easier: Start with the prop already partly open and reward less movement. Avoid unstable furniture and hard resistance.

skills.title: Name response in new settings
skills.goal: Apply the already learned name response to specified easier new contexts.
skills.setup: Record each context separately; this does not change the original name-learning status.

steps.title: Change rooms, keep everything easy
steps.teach: In a second quiet familiar room, let your dog look slightly away, say the name once, and reward the head turn. Start closer and with a smaller angle than the original lesson. If needed, do a few easy name–reward pairings before checking the response again.
steps.advance: Responds on 4 of 5 opportunities in two sessions in the named second room.
steps.easier: Return to immediate pairings or reduce the angle. Record this room, rather than claiming every new setting is covered.

steps.title: Try a quiet secure outdoor place
steps.teach: Use a quiet fenced yard or a secure leash/harness setup. Wait for a comfortable moment with little happening; say the name once and reward the turn. Keep rewards generous and sessions short. Let the dog return to sniffing after success.
steps.advance: Responds on 4 of 5 easy opportunities across two sessions in this specific outdoor setting.
steps.easier: Use a quieter spot, shorter distance, or return indoors. Do not repeat louder if they are worried.

steps.title: Add one mild controlled distraction
steps.teach: In the successful setting, add an unimportant mild distraction, such as a familiar person moving slowly far away. Ask once while the dog is still comfortable and reward the turn. Increase only one variable on later sessions. Anxiety triggers should first have their own emotional-learning work.
steps.advance: Responds on 4 of 5 comfortable opportunities in two sessions at the recorded distraction level.
steps.easier: Remove the distraction or increase distance. High stress is not a required graduation test.

skills.title: Recall in a new safe setting
skills.goal: Apply recall outdoors while retaining physical safety.
skills.setup: Long line on a comfortable harness; secure area; no line wrapped around hands or neck.

steps.title: Restart short in a quiet outdoor area
steps.teach: Begin much closer than your best indoor recall, with the line slack and the dog comfortable. Call once, step back invitingly, reward arrival generously, then let them explore again. Manage the line so it cannot snag or build up a fast hard stop.
steps.advance: Returns over the chosen short outdoor distance in 4 of 5 attempts across two sessions.
steps.easier: Return to a shorter distance or quieter enclosed area; do not reel the dog in as a training response.

steps.title: Change distance or mild interest separately
steps.teach: Once the easy outdoor return is reliable, try a little more distance OR call from an ordinary mild sniff. Keep the other variable easy and reward generously. Do not use a known frightening trigger or a running animal as the next test. Maintain the line for safety.
steps.advance: Reliable comfortable returns in the exact recorded context across two sessions; physical management remains in place.
steps.easier: Reduce the chosen variable. A learned recall does not authorize off-leash exposure near roads or animals.

skills.title: Mat comfort in another place
skills.goal: Use the familiar mat and relaxation routine in a specified easier new setting.
skills.setup: Start with a quiet room, not a busy cafe or trigger-filled park.

steps.title: Transfer the familiar mat
steps.teach: Move the familiar mat to another quiet room. Begin beside it, reward a voluntary approach, then use the known mat cue. Keep any stay very brief. If the dog needs help, teach the easy approach again without changing the original MAT progress.
steps.advance: Goes to the mat comfortably on the cue in the named new room on 4 of 5 attempts across two sessions.
steps.easier: Choose a more familiar room, shorten distance, or reward offered approaches.

steps.title: Rebuild a restful interval
steps.teach: Sit near the mat in this new quiet place and reward voluntary soft resting as in SETTLE. Begin with brief intervals and no other challenges. Later add one small ordinary household movement while shortening duration again. Record the actual setting and movement.
steps.advance: Shows comfortable voluntary rest for the selected short interval in two sessions; soft posture, not rigid waiting.
steps.easier: Remove movement or return to shorter resting periods. Do not station the dog where they need to retreat.

skills.title: Loose walking in another place
skills.goal: Transfer comfortable leash skills to one new low-distraction location.
skills.setup: Secure comfortable equipment; broad paths and exits.

steps.title: Restart with one or two steps
steps.teach: Choose a quiet familiar-adjacent place, such as the yard edge. Reward the known side position, then one or two slack-leash steps. Allow sniff breaks and keep the route short. Treat the new location as a fresh easy version rather than demanding your longest indoor stretch.
steps.advance: Several short loose stretches are comfortable across two sessions in the recorded location.
steps.easier: Use fewer steps or a quieter place; separate fear-driven pulling from ordinary loose-leash practice.

steps.title: Add ordinary variation carefully
steps.teach: Build a few more steps OR one mild ordinary environmental change, keeping the other variable easy. Reward early enough to prevent repeated tight-leash practice. If a trigger appears, use distance and your planned exit instead of holding position to finish the exercise.
steps.advance: Practical loose stretches are comfortable in the named context over two sessions, with easy sniff breaks.
steps.easier: Return to the previous step count or location. Record a different context separately.

skills.title: Maintain skills and review changes
skills.goal: Keep useful cues rewarding and adapt to changing comfort.
skills.setup: Select a few useful skills; do not retest everything in one session.

steps.title: Plan short enjoyable refreshers
steps.teach: Choose one familiar useful skill and one optional fun activity in an easy setting. Reward generously and finish after a few good repetitions. Alternate activities across days if desired. Mark known skills consistent after an easy confirmation rather than retraining all steps unnecessarily.
steps.advance: A manageable refresher routine is recorded and remains enjoyable; no mandatory daily quota.
steps.easier: Use a single easy success and rest. More repetitions are not automatically better.

steps.title: Review one trigger in comparable conditions
steps.teach: Use the session log to compare the same trigger and similar settings over time. Look at posture, comfort, and recovery, not just whether a cue was obeyed. If behavior worsens, reduce challenge, review health and environment, and seek help when needed.
steps.advance: A specific next adjustment is written from comparable observations; unanswered concerns have an appropriate follow-up.
steps.easier: Collect clearer observations at an easier level; leave unknown recovery values blank rather than entering zero.

skills.title: Take a little bow
skills.goal: Offer a brief comfortable play-bow shape.
skills.setup: Healthy comfortable movement on a non-slip floor. Capture a natural stretch; skip for pain, stiffness, or balance concerns.

steps.title: Catch a natural stretch
steps.teach: Watch during an ordinary relaxed transition from rest. If the dog naturally stretches their front end down with the rear up, quietly mark the shape and offer a reward as they stand again. Never push the chest down or hold the back end up.
steps.advance: You can reward several naturally offered comfortable bows without interrupting rest.
steps.easier: Skip this trick if the movement is rare or uncomfortable. Do not wake or repeatedly provoke stretching.

steps.title: Invite the familiar shape
steps.teach: In a short playful session, wait for a small offered front-end dip and reward it. A gentle empty-hand gesture toward the space between the front paws can become a prompt if the dog willingly follows it. Release promptly rather than asking for a long stretch.
steps.advance: Offers a brief comfortable bow from the gesture in 4 of 5 easy opportunities.
steps.easier: Reward a smaller dip, reset to stand, or return to capturing. Do not place a hand under the abdomen.

steps.title: Name the bow
steps.teach: Say “bow” just before the familiar gesture. Mark the brief shape, release, and reward. Over several enjoyable repetitions make the gesture smaller. End after a few comfortable bows; the aim is a cheerful trick, not a flexibility exercise.
steps.advance: Responds to the cue plus small gesture in two short sessions without strain or prolonged holding.
steps.easier: Keep the original gesture or choose another trick. Stop for any stiffness or reluctance.

skills.title: Stand between your legs
skills.goal: Choose a roomy position between your stationary legs.
skills.setup: Only if the dog fits with generous clearance and the handler is steady; otherwise use a cone game.

steps.title: Make one comfortable pass
steps.teach: Stand with a stable, comfortably wide stance. Offer a familiar hand target so the dog can choose to pass straight through the open space. Reward after they emerge. Keep your legs still and never close them around the dog.
steps.advance: Makes relaxed straight passes with no ducking, squeezing, or hesitation.
steps.easier: Use two widely spaced cones instead, or reward approaching the opening without passing.

steps.title: Pause in the middle
steps.teach: Use a target to guide a familiar easy pass, then reward when the dog is centered between your still legs. Feed at a comfortable forward head position, release after a moment, and let them walk out. Add “middle” before the familiar invitation.
steps.advance: Enters and pauses briefly on cue in 4 of 5 relaxed opportunities.
steps.easier: Reward a complete pass without stopping. Skip if close body space worries either participant.

skills.title: A slow figure eight
skills.goal: Walk a gentle stationary figure eight around your legs.
skills.setup: Generous body clearance and a steady handler; wide curves only. Cone figure eights are an alternative.

steps.title: Make one roomy loop
steps.teach: With your feet still and wide, use the known hand target to invite a comfortable pass, then a broad curve around one leg back to the front. Reward partway at first, then after one complete loop. Avoid wrapping tightly against the knee or dog’s body.
steps.advance: Completes one smooth unhurried loop without squeezing or physical steering.
steps.easier: Make a larger curve or use a cone. Stop if the handler must balance or move abruptly.

steps.title: Learn the other loop
steps.teach: Practice a separate roomy loop around the other leg using the other hand target. Reward that loop on its own until it is familiar. Alternate which side starts, but do not link the loops yet if either direction feels awkward.
steps.advance: Offers either single loop comfortably from its hand signal in two short sessions.
steps.easier: Practice the easier side once and finish; reduce bending demands rather than drilling the difficult side.

steps.title: Join the figure eight
steps.teach: Guide one familiar loop and switch to the other target for the second. Reward after the first loop if needed, then after both when joining is easy. Add “weave” before the first signal. Keep the sequence slow and end with an easy release.
steps.advance: Completes one comfortable figure eight from the cue and small hand signals in 4 of 5 easy attempts.
steps.easier: Reward each loop separately or return to cone loops. No fast repetitions or tight turns.

skills.title: Roll a ball with the nose
skills.goal: Nudge a safe large ball along the floor.
skills.setup: A lightweight ball far too large to swallow; clear flat non-slip floor; no hard or tiny balls.

steps.title: Find a gentle nose touch
steps.teach: Hold the large ball still just below natural nose height. Mark a voluntary nose touch and reward from your other hand. Keep the ball steady and reward gentle contact rather than grabbing. If the dog prefers to bite it, choose a larger ball or another game.
steps.advance: Offers gentle nose contacts in 4 of 5 comfortable presentations.
steps.easier: Use a familiar target on the ball’s near side or reward a glance. Stop if the ball worries them.

steps.title: Let a small nudge move it
steps.teach: Rest the ball on the floor against your foot so it cannot roll far. Reward a nose touch, then let a tiny nudge move it an inch or two. Reset calmly. Gradually allow a slightly longer roll without encouraging chasing or pouncing.
steps.advance: Uses the nose to roll the ball a short distance several times without grabbing or frantic chasing.
steps.easier: Stabilize it again or reward a stationary touch. Use an even lighter oversized ball.

steps.title: Cue one short roll
steps.teach: Say “push” before the familiar nudge. Mark and reward a short floor roll, then stop the ball and reset. Gradually fade your pointing so the cue and ball presentation invite the action. Keep the reward close and the activity slow.
steps.advance: Produces one controlled nose roll on cue in two short sessions.
steps.easier: Return to one tiny movement. End before the game turns into intense chasing.

skills.title: Dog bowling
skills.goal: Nudge a large ball toward a few soft lightweight pins.
skills.setup: Known ball push; two or three soft pins that fall quietly; no chewable small pieces.

steps.title: One quiet pin
steps.teach: Place one soft pin close behind the known ball, leaving a straight easy route. Cue the familiar nose roll. Reward movement toward the pin even if it misses; separately reward comfortable responses to a quiet fall. Reset the pin yourself after each attempt.
steps.advance: Rolls toward the nearby pin and stays comfortable when it falls softly.
steps.easier: Remove the pin or make it quieter. Return to stationary ball touches if the fall startles the dog.

steps.title: A small bowling lane
steps.teach: Arrange two or three familiar quiet pins in a wide close cluster. Put the ball on the easy straight route and cue one roll. Mark a roll into the cluster, reward, and reset. Increase distance only slightly once aiming is comfortable.
steps.advance: Makes several purposeful short rolls toward the soft pins, with comfortable resets and no grabbing.
steps.easier: Use one closer pin or reward near misses. Winning a strike is optional; enjoyment is the criterion.

skills.title: Score a gentle goal
skills.goal: Nose-roll a safe ball between two floor markers.
skills.setup: Two widely spaced soft markers and a known oversized ball; no nets or entanglement hazards.

steps.title: A wide nearby opening
steps.teach: Set two soft markers far apart just beyond the ball. Cue a short familiar nose roll toward the open gap and reward movement into it. Start close enough that aiming is easy; do not ask for a chase, forceful impact, or several pushes in a row.
steps.advance: Comfortably rolls the ball through the wide nearby gap several times.
steps.easier: Widen the goal or move it closer. Reward a roll toward the gap first.

steps.title: Name the little game
steps.teach: Say “goal” before the familiar push cue, then gradually use the new cue with a small pointing gesture. Reward one successful short roll and reset. If desired, move the start position a few inches; treat that as a separate small adjustment.
steps.advance: Offers one controlled roll toward and through the familiar opening on cue in two sessions.
steps.easier: Return to a close wide goal and known push cue. No need for harder shots or prolonged repetitions.

skills.title: Low high five
skills.goal: Briefly touch a low open palm with a front paw.
skills.setup: A stable comfortable position; hand kept below the dog’s elbow, with no paw pulling.

steps.title: Change the paw target
steps.teach: Offer the familiar paw invitation with your palm more upright but still low. Mark a light voluntary paw contact and reward. Remove your hand after a moment rather than holding the paw. Reward a small lift if the changed hand shape is puzzling.
steps.advance: Makes gentle low palm contact without leaning, twisting, or having the paw held.
steps.easier: Return to the known paw cue and horizontal hand. Skip if balancing on three legs is uncomfortable.

steps.title: Add the new cue
steps.teach: Say “high five” before presenting the low upright palm. Mark the brief touch, lower your hand, and reward. Gradually reduce the older paw prompt. Keep the hand low; the name of the trick does not require lifting the limb high.
steps.advance: Offers a brief low paw touch in 4 of 5 easy invitations across two short sessions.
steps.easier: Keep the clearer old signal or reward a smaller lift. Do not repeat through fatigue.

skills.title: A little wave
skills.goal: Offer one small paw lift without hand contact.
skills.setup: Comfortable balanced position and known low high five; no repeated high paw lifts.

steps.title: Reward the lift before contact
steps.teach: Invite the familiar low high five. As the paw begins to lift, mark before it reaches your palm, lower your hand away, and reward. Keep the movement small so the dog does not stretch or paw at your arm. Reset between attempts.
steps.advance: Offers a small comfortable paw lift when shown the familiar hand signal.
steps.easier: Reward ordinary low palm contact again. Do not withdraw the hand so fast that the dog overreaches.

steps.title: Name one small wave
steps.teach: Say “wave,” give a smaller version of the familiar signal, and reward one short lift. Gradually hold your signal farther from the paw while still easy to understand. One lift is enough; repeated waving and elevated holds are not required.
steps.advance: Responds to cue and small signal with a balanced low paw lift in two short sessions.
steps.easier: Return to low high five or choose a nose-target trick if paw lifting is uncomfortable.

skills.title: A comfortable photo pose
skills.goal: Hold a chosen comfortable position for a quick photo.
skills.setup: Use a known comfortable sit or stand; no costumes, forced handling, flash, or startling props.

steps.title: A very short still moment
steps.teach: Invite a comfortable familiar sit or stand. Mark a brief still moment and reward before your dog needs to move. Hold the phone down at first and reward comfort with it being present. Keep looking at your dog rather than repeatedly rearranging them.
steps.advance: Offers one or two comfortable still seconds with the ordinary phone present.
steps.easier: Use stand instead of sit, keep the phone farther away, or reward any comfortable pause.

steps.title: Pair a quiet photo with a cue
steps.teach: Say “pose” before the familiar position signal. Reward a brief pause, then take one silent no-flash photo and release. On later attempts reward immediately after the photo. Keep the phone’s motion small and give the dog a choice to finish.
steps.advance: Comfortably pauses for one quick no-flash photo in several easy attempts.
steps.easier: Return to phone presence without taking a picture. A photo is never worth extending discomfort.

skills.title: Give one toy a name
skills.goal: Build a playful association with one designated toy’s label.
skills.setup: One safe favorite toy in a quiet room; this experiment is optional and does not test intelligence.

steps.title: Use the label during play
steps.teach: Choose one short label for the favorite toy. Say it once as you present the toy for a brief game the dog already enjoys. Repeat on separate playful occasions, not in a long naming drill. Keep other toys out of these initial pairings.
steps.advance: The dog enjoys repeated brief label-and-toy play pairings without frustration.
steps.easier: Use ordinary unnamed play. Object labels are difficult for many dogs, and this is entirely optional.

steps.title: Request that one familiar toy
steps.teach: Put only the named toy nearby on a clear floor. Say its label once, then invite the familiar pickup if needed. Reward delivery or a clear approach. Gradually reduce the pickup gesture while moving the toy to a few obvious nearby spots.
steps.advance: Approaches or retrieves the single named toy from several easy nearby placements. This does not yet establish label discrimination.
steps.easier: Return to playful pairings or ordinary fetch. Do not claim understanding from a one-object setup.

skills.title: An optional two-toy choice
skills.goal: Explore whether two toy labels guide choices without position or pointing cues.
skills.setup: Two safe familiar toys with distinct labels; neutral body position; optional helper to place objects.

steps.title: Build the second toy association
steps.teach: Use a second distinct safe toy and its own short label during enjoyable brief play, just as for the first. Practice each toy separately in varied easy positions. Keep sessions playful and stop if the dog appears to be guessing repeatedly or becoming frustrated.
steps.advance: The second toy has enjoyable label pairings and easy single-toy approach or retrieve practice.
steps.easier: Continue ordinary toy play with either object. There is no deadline for learning labels.

steps.title: Offer a fair close choice
steps.teach: Place both familiar toys a short equal distance away, then stand centered with still hands and neutral gaze. Say one label once. Reward the requested choice; after an error, reset to an easy single-toy success rather than correcting or repeatedly testing.
steps.advance: Shows several comfortable choices that appear related to the requested label, with no pressure or escalating errors.
steps.easier: Return to one toy and playful pairings. Frequent errors are information, not disobedience.

steps.title: Check sides and human cues
steps.teach: Use a helper to swap toy sides between easy trials while you remain centered. Request each label in a mixed order, avoiding a predictable left–right pattern. Record choices before interpreting success. If side preference or gestures explain the choices, keep the game as ordinary fetch.
steps.advance: Across two brief mixed-position sets, most choices follow the requested label rather than side or pointing. No vocabulary or intelligence claim follows from this small check.
steps.easier: Reduce tests or stop if enjoyment drops. Gifted word-learning research does not promise this ability in every dog.

skills.title: Respond to picture cue cards
skills.goal: Explore two visual symbols as cues for already known actions.
skills.setup: Large cards held still; two comfortable known actions such as sit and nose touch. This is visual cue learning, not reading language.

steps.title: Pair one symbol with one known action
steps.teach: Show a large simple circle card briefly, then give the familiar cue for a comfortable known sit or stand. Reward the action and put the card away. After several easy pairings, pause briefly after showing it to see whether the action is offered before the old cue.
steps.advance: The first card begins to prompt its paired known action without repeated verbal requests.
steps.easier: Keep the usual verbal cue or stop the experiment. Never physically position the dog.

steps.title: Pair the other symbol separately
steps.teach: On separate easy repetitions show a very different symbol, such as thick stripes, before a familiar nose-touch cue. Reward the known touch and remove the card. Keep the picture-to-action pairing consistent; do not add novelty, distance, or distracting settings yet.
steps.advance: The second symbol begins to prompt its separate familiar action in a comfortable easy setup.
steps.easier: Use more distinct large symbols or return to ordinary cues. Avoid piling up unsuccessful guesses.

steps.title: Alternate without hidden help
steps.teach: Present one card at a time in the same central position and a mixed order. Keep voice, posture, and hand position neutral until the dog responds. Reward the paired action. If the old cues are still doing the work, keep practicing or choose a simpler trick.
steps.advance: Usually offers the paired action for each card across two brief mixed-order sessions. This is not evidence of literacy.
steps.easier: Re-pair each symbol separately. Any enjoyable learning is sufficient; no tests under pressure.

skills.title: Back up a few steps
skills.goal: Take one to three comfortable backward steps without being crowded.
skills.setup: Flat non-slip space with an unobstructed route; no narrow chute, leash pressure, or approach into the dog.

steps.title: Reward a backward foot shift
steps.teach: Begin with the dog standing comfortably in open space. After an ordinary reward, watch for a voluntary small backward weight shift or foot movement as they reset. Mark it immediately and deliver the next reward where they can remain balanced. Stay still rather than stepping into them.
steps.advance: Offers several small backward foot movements without sitting, scrambling, or being crowded.
steps.easier: Reward a weight shift first, keep sessions very short, or skip if the dog cannot find a comfortable movement.

steps.title: Build one clear step
steps.teach: Reward the familiar backward shift, then wait for a slightly larger movement that places one foot back. Mark that movement and reward. Once a clear step is offered, say “back” just before it. Keep your own feet stationary and the route open.
steps.advance: Takes one voluntary step back on the emerging cue in 4 of 5 easy attempts.
steps.easier: Return to a tiny shift. Check the surface and stop for stiffness or confusion.

steps.title: Add a second step
steps.teach: Cue one known backward step, then briefly wait for a second before marking and rewarding. Mix one-step rewards with occasional two-step attempts. Only later invite three slow steps. This is a short positioning game, not a speed or endurance drill.
steps.advance: Offers two or three balanced steps on cue in two short sessions.
steps.easier: Reward the first step again. Do not chase the dog backward or practice near edges.

skills.title: Go around a cone
skills.goal: Walk a broad loop around one floor marker.
skills.setup: A stable soft cone or broad safe object; clear non-slip space.

steps.title: Follow a wide arc
steps.teach: Place the cone several feet away in clear space. Use a known hand target to invite the dog along a broad half-circle around it. Reward at the far side, then guide the remaining half. Keep the curve wide enough for ordinary walking without twisting.
steps.advance: Comfortably completes the loop with two reward points and no contact with the cone.
steps.easier: Use a smaller arc, more space, or remove a novel cone until the dog is comfortable.

steps.title: Join and name the loop
steps.teach: Use the familiar arc with fewer target presentations until the dog can walk the whole loop before the reward. Say “around” before the gesture. Gradually reduce your own movement while keeping the cone close and the route broad.
steps.advance: Walks one full broad loop from a cue and gesture in 4 of 5 easy attempts.
steps.easier: Walk with the dog again or reward halfway. Transfer to other places belongs in separate easy practice.

skills.title: Figure eight around two markers
skills.goal: Join two broad cone loops into one smooth figure eight.
skills.setup: Two soft stable markers spaced generously apart; comfortable walking only.

steps.title: Practice each separate loop
steps.teach: Place two familiar markers far enough apart for a wide walking curve. Cue a known loop around one, reward, and pause. Practice the other marker separately. Use a hand target for help rather than tightening the dog’s path with your body.
steps.advance: Can complete either separate broad loop comfortably with clear signals.
steps.easier: Increase the gap or return to one marker. Skip tight turns or repetitive bending.

steps.title: Connect the loops
steps.teach: Guide one easy loop, then point through the open center toward the second marker for another loop. Reward in the center at first. As joining becomes easy, reward after the whole figure eight and add your chosen cue before starting.
steps.advance: Completes a slow broad figure eight with comfortable movement in two short sessions.
steps.easier: Reward the center transition, use a bigger layout, or return to separate loops.

skills.title: Front paws on a flat target
skills.goal: Place both front feet on a stable floor mat.
skills.setup: A broad non-slip mat lying flat, with no raised or unstable platform.

steps.title: Find one paw contact
steps.teach: Lay the mat flat in an open room and let the dog investigate. Mark any voluntary front-paw contact and deliver a reward while the paw is still there if comfortable. Release or toss a nearby reset reward so the dog can choose another approach.
steps.advance: Voluntarily places at least one front paw on the mat on several approaches.
steps.easier: Use a larger mat or reward approaching it. Never lift a paw or pull the dog onto it.

steps.title: Reward two front paws
steps.teach: When one-paw contacts are easy, reward approaches that bring both front paws onto the broad mat. Deliver food at a comfortable natural head height so the dog can stand balanced. Keep all feet on the floor and release after a brief moment.
steps.advance: Offers both front paws on the mat in 4 of 5 easy approaches.
steps.easier: Reward one paw again, enlarge the target, or stop for any uneven or uncomfortable movement.

steps.title: Add the floor-target cue
steps.teach: Say “feet” before the familiar invitation toward the mat. Mark two front paws, reward, then release. Fade pointing a little at a time. The goal is this safe flat target; raising it or adding unstable surfaces is not part of this lesson.
steps.advance: Places both front feet on the familiar floor target from the cue in two short sessions.
steps.easier: Keep the clear gesture or larger target. Do not progress to balance equipment without individual guidance.

skills.title: Walk through a floor-level hoop
skills.goal: Choose to walk through a large opening without jumping.
skills.setup: A very wide smooth hoop held stationary with its bottom resting on the floor; no collars or tags that can snag.

steps.title: Explore the open shape
steps.teach: Keep the hoop still with its bottom on the floor and plenty of room to go around it. Reward a glance or approach. If comfortable, offer a hand target through the center and reward one voluntary step through. Never move the hoop over the dog.
steps.advance: Walks through the large opening comfortably while it stays stationary on the floor.
steps.easier: Use a wider opening or stop at looking. Avoid hoops if tags, equipment, or body shape could snag.

steps.title: Name the walking pass
steps.teach: Say “through” before the familiar target invitation. Reward after the dog walks fully through. Gradually reduce your hand movement while the hoop remains on the floor. Reset away from it so each pass is voluntary rather than a repetitive obstacle circuit.
steps.advance: Makes a relaxed walking pass on cue in 4 of 5 attempts across two short sessions.
steps.easier: Use the target again or end. This lesson does not add height, jumping, or narrow openings.

skills.title: Explore an open tunnel
skills.goal: Choose a short, wide, secured open tunnel.
skills.setup: A wide rigid/open-ended dog tunnel secured against rolling; start extremely short or fully open. A helper may steady equipment, never hold the dog.

steps.title: Explore without entering
steps.teach: Set the tunnel where the dog can investigate and walk away. Reward looking or approaching the entrance, with rewards placed outside first. Keep the interior bright and the far end visible. If the dog avoids it, simply give more space and finish there.
steps.advance: Approaches the entrance with ordinary loose movement and freely leaves and returns.
steps.easier: Use a large open arch instead. Do not lure an uneasy dog inside or block the exit.

steps.title: Take one voluntary short pass
steps.teach: Use the shortest open version with your reward hand visible just beyond the other end. Let the dog choose a straight walking pass and reward after they emerge. Reset outside. Keep the tunnel fixed and do not touch or move it while the dog is inside.
steps.advance: Chooses several relaxed short passes without crouching, rushing, freezing, or scrambling.
steps.easier: Shorten or widen the opening. Skip if a comfortable version is unavailable.

steps.title: Add a cue before the pass
steps.teach: Say “tunnel” before the familiar easy invitation. Reward each voluntary pass, then reduce the invitation slightly. Only add a tiny amount of straight tunnel length when both ends remain obvious. Keep curved, long, dark, or collapsible fabric tunnels outside this plan.
steps.advance: Comfortably enters the familiar short open tunnel on cue in two easy sessions.
steps.easier: Return to the shorter version or a floor-level hoop; no pushing, chasing, or trapping.

skills.title: Open this refrigerator
skills.goal: Open one approved refrigerator gently, under supervision.
skills.setup: Clear food access, non-slip footing, reachable handle; remove rope outside sessions. Skip a stiff seal.

steps.title: Make refrigerator movement comfortable
steps.teach: Without any pulling task, stand at a comfortable distance from the closed fridge. Open it a tiny amount, then feed your dog and close gently. Separately pair any light/compressor sounds that matter. Allow retreat. Do not train pulling while door movement itself worries the dog.
steps.advance: Comfortable with gentle opening, light, and sound in several observations across two sessions.
steps.easier: Use smaller movement or more distance. Continue with a human-opened retrieval if the appliance is unsuitable.

steps.title: Use the rope with the door already ajar
steps.teach: Attach the familiar handle securely where it cannot catch the dog. Begin with the fridge door a little ajar so almost no force is needed. Cue pull; reward the smallest useful opening and a release. Stand ready to control the door’s swing without trapping the dog.
steps.advance: Can open the ajar door gently and release the rope on 4 of 5 attempts across two sessions.
steps.easier: Increase the starting gap or return to the lightweight prop. Do not reward hard jerks or chewing.

steps.title: Reduce the starting gap carefully
steps.teach: Decrease the initial gap slightly on an easy repetition, keeping the pull gentle. Alternate with ajar starts. Attempt the actual closed seal only if it releases easily with this gentle motion; otherwise stop at a human-opened door. Add “open” before the known pull when predictable.
steps.advance: Opens this approved easy door from the chosen start on 4 of 5 attempts in two sessions, without strain.
steps.easier: Restore an ajar start or have the human open it. This does not authorize opening other household doors.

skills.title: Nose-push a door closed
skills.goal: Gently push an approved door using a nose target.
skills.setup: A secure large target; no mouth pulling, pinching, slamming, or jumping.

steps.title: Transfer a nose target to a large pad
steps.teach: Present the familiar broad target pad near a stationary approved lightweight door. Reward gentle nose contact while you hold it still. Attach the pad securely at a comfortable nose height, then reward the same touch without moving the door. Keep paws and tail clear; door motion is a separate next step.
steps.advance: Touches the pad gently on 4 of 5 presentations across two sessions.
steps.easier: Show the pad next to the hand again or reward a small nose approach.

steps.title: Add a tiny moving-door push
steps.teach: Put the secure target at nose height on an easy lightweight door, with your hand controlling motion. Start almost closed. Reward a nose touch that moves it only an inch; protect paws and tail. Gradually ask for just enough push to close softly.
steps.advance: Can gently close the lightweight practice door on most attempts without pawing or slamming.
steps.easier: Reduce the gap and support the door more. Stop if motion or sound is worrying.

steps.title: Transfer to this fridge and fade the pad
steps.teach: On the approved fridge, start almost closed and use the same secure nose target with your hand controlling the swing. Reward soft closure. Add “close” before the touch, then make the pad smaller across sessions if safe. Check the seal yourself; never put the dog inside or between door and cabinet.
steps.advance: Softly closes this fridge from the chosen small gap on 4 of 5 attempts in two sessions; a human confirms closure.
steps.easier: Keep the larger target or smaller gap. Human closure is a valid simpler alternative.

skills.title: Retrieve a drink carrier from a shelf
skills.goal: Retrieve a lightweight sealed prop by a suitable carry handle.
skills.setup: Sealed water bottle in a robust suitable carrier; never glass or a bare can in the mouth. No alcohol ingestion.

steps.title: Practice the actual carrier near you
steps.teach: Use a lightweight sealed water-bottle prop inside a robust suitable carrier with a safe grasping handle. Ask for the known take, brief hold, and give, rewarding each delivery. Inspect for chewing or punctures. A beer-style routine uses the same action; the dog never opens or drinks the contents.
steps.advance: Takes and delivers the protected prop gently on most easy attempts; no chewing or damage.
steps.easier: Use an empty lighter carrier or ordinary toy. If the dog crushes, punctures, or guards it, skip this module.

steps.title: Pick up from an easy mock shelf
steps.teach: Place the carrier on a stable low surface at a natural mouth height, directly next to you. Cue fetch, receive with give, and reward. Gradually add a step of carrying. The dog keeps all paws on the floor; no jumping, climbing, or stretching into a deep shelf.
steps.advance: Picks up from this reachable surface and delivers gently on 4 of 5 attempts in two sessions.
steps.easier: Move the carrier nearer the shelf edge or use a lower stable surface.

steps.title: Transfer to the already-open fridge
steps.teach: Have a human hold the fridge door safely open. Remove other reachable food and place only the carrier on an easy reachable shelf. Stand close, cue the known pickup, receive, and reward. Add a few delivery steps gradually; keep opening and closing out of this lesson.
steps.advance: Retrieves from the open approved fridge and delivers gently on 4 of 5 attempts in two sessions.
steps.easier: Return to the mock shelf or an empty carrier. Use supervision and prevent unsupervised appliance access.

skills.title: Press a large quiet button
skills.goal: Press a broad stable pad with the nose.
skills.setup: A large low-force muted training button or inert practice pad; no cables, batteries, small parts, or startling sound within reach.

steps.title: Target the pad
steps.teach: Keep the pad stable at a comfortable nose height. Reward voluntary nose contact, as with an ordinary object target. Choose a target too large to mouth or swallow and keep any electronic mechanism inaccessible. Teach with the sound disabled first.
steps.advance: Touches the stable pad with a relaxed nose on several presentations.
steps.easier: Use a flat inert pad or ordinary target. End if the dog paws, mouths, or avoids it.

steps.title: Add only gentle pressure
steps.teach: Reward touches that slightly depress the low-force pad. Mark as the surface moves and reward from the other hand. If pressure is difficult, use a more sensitive pad rather than asking the dog to push harder or brace their neck.
steps.advance: Produces a gentle clear press repeatedly without strain, grabbing, or startle.
steps.easier: Return to light touch on an inert pad. No hard switches or forceful repeated pushes.

steps.title: Use the designated button cue
steps.teach: Say “button” before offering the familiar pad. Reward one press and reset. Fade pointing while the pad remains in its familiar position. Optional sound is a separate gradual comfort lesson; this action alone is not evidence of language or a request.
steps.advance: Gently presses the designated pad on cue in two short sessions.
steps.easier: Keep it muted and use the old target cue. Skip sound if noises are a concern.

skills.title: Bring a designated slipper
skills.goal: Fetch one safe training slipper into your hand.
skills.setup: A clean light oversized slipper with no loose parts; skip for dogs that shred, swallow fabric, or guard items.

steps.title: Make the safe prop familiar
steps.teach: Present the designated slipper as a training prop and invite a known take. Reward a gentle hold, then ask for the familiar give into your hand. Use one supervised prop consistently; do not encourage searching the household for other shoes.
steps.advance: Takes and gives the designated prop gently without chewing, guarding, or tugging.
steps.easier: Use a familiar safe toy instead. Stop if any part could be swallowed or the dog guards it.

steps.title: Pick it up nearby
steps.teach: Place the slipper on a clear non-slip floor close to your feet. Invite a known pickup and delivery, then reward the give into your hand. If needed, practice the pickup alone before asking for the return. Reset yourself after every attempt.
steps.advance: Picks up and gives the nearby prop in 4 of 5 easy opportunities.
steps.easier: Bring it closer or present it at hand height again. Reward smaller comfortable parts.

steps.title: Retrieve from one designated spot
steps.teach: Put the slipper on an obvious low mat a few steps away. Say “slipper” before the familiar retrieve invitation. Reward delivery, then return it to that same spot. Increase only a step at a time and keep all other footwear out of the game.
steps.advance: Retrieves this prop from its designated easy spot and gives it to you in two sessions.
steps.easier: Return to a shorter distance or a safe toy. General household scavenging is not part of this job.

skills.title: Carry a little pouch
skills.goal: Carry a safe light message pouch a short distance.
skills.setup: A soft oversized empty pouch with a broad safe grip; no straps that can loop over the head and no contents to ingest.

steps.title: Take and return the empty pouch
steps.teach: Offer the familiar safe grip area and cue a known take. Mark a gentle hold, then ask for give and reward. Keep the pouch empty while introducing its feel. The dog should not need to grip a zipper, buckle, or narrow cord.
steps.advance: Takes, gently holds, and gives the empty pouch with no chewing or worry.
steps.easier: Use an ordinary safe retrieve toy. Remove straps or choose a different prop.

steps.title: Carry toward a nearby hand
steps.teach: Offer the empty pouch, take one slow step back, and invite the familiar give into your hand. Reward after delivery. Build only a few steps, keeping the pouch off the ground and the route clear without asking for a prolonged hold.
steps.advance: Comfortably carries the empty pouch a few steps and gives on cue.
steps.easier: Return to a stationary give or one step. Stop if the load or grip changes natural movement.

steps.title: One light protected note
steps.teach: If the pouch is designed to stay closed and your dog is not a shredder, add a single protected paper note with no staples or clips. Repeat the familiar short carry. The human handles opening and closing; the dog only transports the safe prop.
steps.advance: Carries the very light closed pouch and gives it reliably without chewing or inspecting the contents.
steps.easier: Keep it empty or use a toy messenger game. Never add medication, valuables, or heavy contents.

skills.title: Deliver to a familiar person
skills.goal: Carry a safe toy or pouch to one cooperative familiar adult.
skills.setup: Two trusted adults close together; a safe carry prop; no guarding or tension around people.

steps.title: Give to the second adult
steps.teach: Have the familiar helper sit or stand nearby without reaching over the dog. Let them invite the known give into an open low hand and reward the delivery. Begin while you are still beside the dog so no departure or stranger approach is involved.
steps.advance: Comfortably gives the safe prop to the familiar helper without guarding or hesitation.
steps.easier: Use the usual person for give first. Stop if hand approaches or item possession creates tension.

steps.title: Carry one step toward the helper
steps.teach: Offer the familiar safe prop, then let the nearby helper invite delivery with the known open hand. Reward after the give. Start one step apart and gradually make it a few steps, with both people still visible and relaxed.
steps.advance: Carries and gives to the nearby helper on their invitation in several easy attempts.
steps.easier: Bring the helper closer, use a safer toy, or practice separate give repetitions again.

steps.title: Start the message job
steps.teach: Say “deliver” before the helper’s familiar invitation. Gradually make their hand signal smaller while keeping them clearly visible. Reward the give and celebrate with a quiet break. This is a specific cooperative game, not permission to approach unfamiliar people with objects.
steps.advance: Completes the short take–carry–give sequence to this familiar helper in two sessions.
steps.easier: Return to one-step delivery or ordinary toy fetch. Do not use the game to force social contact.

skills.title: Place safe cloths in a basket
skills.goal: Move designated clean training cloths into a low open basket.
skills.setup: Large safe clean cloth props and a stable low basket; no socks, detergent, dirty laundry, strings, or ingestible fabric for shredders.

steps.title: One cloth over the basket
steps.teach: Offer the safe training cloth just above a wide low basket. Ask for a known take and drop so the cloth falls inside. Mark the drop and reward. Keep hands still and do not pull the cloth from the dog’s mouth.
steps.advance: Drops the designated cloth into the basket comfortably several times.
steps.easier: Use a safe familiar toy or widen the basket. Skip fabric if chewing or swallowing is likely.

steps.title: Pick up beside the basket
steps.teach: Place the same cloth on the floor touching the basket’s outside edge. Invite pickup, then the familiar drop over the rim. Reward that delivery. Practice one cloth at a time, making the path only long enough to connect pickup and drop.
steps.advance: Picks up the nearby cloth and deposits it into the basket in 4 of 5 easy attempts.
steps.easier: Hold the cloth above the basket again, or practice a separate floor pickup first.

steps.title: Gather a small visible set
steps.teach: Place two designated cloths a little apart near the basket. Cue “laundry” for one pickup and deposit, reward, then start a new invitation for the second. Build only short visible routes; humans handle all actual laundry products and appliance access.
steps.advance: Makes two separately cued comfortable deposits from nearby spots without chewing or guarding.
steps.easier: Return to one cloth beside the basket. No repeated drilling or access to laundry machines.

skills.title: Two-toy tidy-up
skills.goal: Put each of two designated toys into its own marked basket.
skills.setup: Two broad low baskets on distinct large markers and two safe familiar toys. Teach particular toy-to-basket pairings; avoid small labels, lids and chewable decorations.

steps.title: First toy and basket
steps.teach: Use only the first toy and its marked basket. Begin with the known basket deposit, reward, then reset. Add a short basket cue before the deposit and build a small approach. Keep this one predictable toy-to-destination pairing throughout practice.
steps.advance: Deposits the first toy into its marked basket from a short approach on its cue.
steps.easier: Work above a wider low basket rim and shorten the carry.

steps.title: Second toy and basket
steps.teach: With the first pair put away, practice the second safe toy and a differently marked basket. Reward easy deposits, then name that destination and add a short approach. This pair can be learned on its own, alongside the first pair.
steps.advance: Deposits the second toy into its own marked basket from a short approach.
steps.easier: Use a close drop again and make the destination markers more distinct.

steps.title: Choose the destination
steps.teach: Put both marked baskets in view. Offer one toy and help with its familiar destination cue, then reduce that prompt when easy. Practice either toy, swap basket positions with their markers and keep your gaze neutral. Reset mistakes to an easy known deposit.
steps.advance: Usually sends each toy to its own basket across swapped positions, with little extra prompting.
steps.easier: Separate the baskets more or practice each toy-to-basket pairing alone.

steps.title: Pick up and tidy both toys
steps.teach: Place the two familiar toys apart on the floor. Invite pickup and the matching deposit, reward, then invite the remaining toy. Let the dog choose the order and reward both deposits. Finish clearly after the small set rather than repeatedly scattering it.
steps.advance: Picks up and deposits both toys into their matching destinations across two short sessions.
steps.easier: Offer one toy at a time and keep the basket cues.

skills.title: A two-person delivery round
skills.goal: Collect a safe pouch, hand it to one designated familiar receiver and return to the sender.
skills.setup: Two familiar willing adults, a safe oversized pouch, broad low tray and flat starting mat. Both adults remain available; no restraint or separation distress.

steps.title: Collect and deliver
steps.teach: Put the familiar pouch on a stable low open tray beside you. Invite pickup and a short known delivery to the visible receiver. They ask for give and reward. Reset together; keep the route short and use an empty pouch first.
steps.advance: Collects from the tray and gently hands the pouch to the nearby receiver.
steps.easier: Offer the pouch from your hand or bring the receiver closer.

steps.title: Return empty to the sender
steps.teach: Without a pouch, have the receiver release the dog toward the sender’s nearby familiar mat. Invite and reward arrival there. Keep both people visible and allow the dog to opt out; this empty return can be learned separately from collection and delivery.
steps.advance: Willingly returns empty to the sender’s mat from the nearby receiver.
steps.easier: Bring the starting mat closer and rehearse its approach without a delivery.

steps.title: Join the round
steps.teach: Invite tray pickup, delivery, give and the empty return using the familiar component cues. Reward the handover and the mat return. Add the round cue just before pickup, allowing a short pause before extra help when the pattern is comfortable.
steps.advance: Connects collection, handover and return on the round cue with helpful component cues as needed.
steps.easier: Rehearse the uncertain component alone and keep rewards at both ends.

steps.title: Vary one feature and finish
steps.teach: Change just the short route, the visible receiver’s standing spot or the adults’ roles, returning to the easiest setup between variations. Deliver a light protected note only inside the familiar pouch. Reward both ends and finish after one round; inspect and remove the props.
steps.advance: Completes a comfortable short round with either adult in the practiced roles and a clear finish.
steps.easier: Keep the original roles, empty pouch and short visible route.

skills.title: A third toy destination
skills.goal: Add a third designated toy-and-basket pairing, then separately teach more examples for each destination.
skills.setup: Three low marked baskets; safe oversized ball, stuffed toy and sturdy supervised rope prop, plus a second suitable example of each if wanted. Skip any toy the dog shreds or swallows.

steps.title: Teach the third pair alone
steps.teach: Put away the first two baskets. Use the third safe toy with its own marked low basket. Rehearse a short known pickup and deposit, reward, and reset. Add a distinctive destination cue while this isolated pairing becomes familiar and predictable.
steps.advance: Delivers the third designated toy to its marked basket from a short distance.
steps.easier: Use a close supported basket deposit again. This pair does not need the other pairs first.

steps.title: Choose among three destinations
steps.teach: Bring back the two familiar marked baskets and start close to the third destination. Offer its toy and cue the known deposit, then practice each old pair. Gradually use equal approaches and swapped positions, rewarding correct destinations without pointing or corrections.
steps.advance: Chooses the matching basket for each of three designated toys across swapped positions.
steps.easier: Return to isolated pairs, greater basket separation or an easier two-basket choice.

steps.title: Teach additional examples explicitly
steps.teach: Introduce one new safe ball with only the ball basket present, then one new stuffed toy with its basket and a new rope prop with its own. Teach every new pairing separately before mixed choices. Similar appearance alone does not establish a sorting rule.
steps.advance: Six individually trained safe objects, two per destination, go to their practiced baskets in mixed choices.
steps.easier: Keep three designated toys. Do not test novel objects repeatedly or claim abstract category understanding.

skills.title: Recognize a familiar person’s name
skills.goal: Use a familiar adult’s spoken name to choose whom to approach, without carrying anything.
skills.cue: Sarah / Alex (use your familiar adults’ names)
skills.setup: Two familiar willing adults and an enclosed quiet room. No strangers, crowds, restraint or social pressure. Adults use neutral hands and do not beckon during choice trials.

steps.title: Pair the first person’s name
steps.teach: With only the first familiar adult nearby, say their name once before an ordinary voluntary approach and reward there. The adult stays still and welcoming. Change their easy standing spot between short turns, using a normal invitation if needed before fading it.
steps.advance: Comfortably approaches the first familiar adult after their name in several easy positions.
steps.easier: Have the adult closer and fully visible; skip approaches the dog does not choose.

steps.title: Pair the second person’s name
steps.teach: Practice separately with the second familiar adult and a distinct spoken name. Pair the name with a comfortable short approach and reward while the first adult is out of the choice area. Vary easy positions and avoid making a particular side part of the cue.
steps.advance: Comfortably approaches the second familiar adult after their name in several easy positions.
steps.easier: Keep only that adult visible and use the familiar approach invitation.

steps.title: Choose by name with both present
steps.teach: Place both familiar adults equally close, with relaxed still hands. Say one name, let the dog choose, and reward at the requested person. After an error make the next turn easier instead of correcting. Swap people’s positions and request both names in mixed order.
steps.advance: Usually chooses either named adult across side swaps and mixed requests without pointing or beckoning.
steps.easier: Return to separate name-and-approach practice and reduce competing distractions.

steps.title: Choose the named person instead of the nearest
steps.teach: Keep both adults fully visible and place one a little farther away. Request the farther adult on an easy turn, then vary requests and swap distances. Reward at the intended adult; help with a close reset before the dog defaults repeatedly to the nearer person.
steps.advance: Choices follow the requested name across changed positions and unequal distances in two brief sessions.
steps.easier: Return to equal distances. This is a practiced two-person discrimination, not recognition of arbitrary names or faces.

skills.title: Retrieve your walk kit
skills.goal: Bring one designated safe carrier holding the walk equipment to the handler.
skills.setup: A large robust carrier with a safe grasp handle; empty first. A human checks that clips, straps and loops stay protected and removes the leash for fitting. Never mouth metal clips or trail loose equipment.

steps.title: Give the carrier to the handler
steps.teach: Offer the empty safe carrier from your hand. Ask for the familiar gentle take and give, reward, and inspect it before another short turn. Keep equipment out until the carrier itself is easy and safe to handle; skip this job for shredders.
steps.advance: Takes and hands the empty carrier back gently without chewing or guarding.
steps.easier: Use an approved familiar retrieve prop or keep equipment collection as the human’s job.

steps.title: Retrieve from its low station
steps.teach: Place the familiar empty carrier on a stable low open surface or clear floor at its designated station. Invite the known pickup, receive with give and reward. Add a few easy carrying steps while keeping all loose clips and straps out of reach.
steps.advance: Retrieves the carrier from the low station and gives it comfortably to the handler.
steps.easier: Return to a hand presentation or put the carrier closer.

steps.title: Bring the protected walk kit
steps.teach: Put only suitable light equipment securely inside the carrier after a human safety check. Rehearse the same short retrieve and give, then the human puts it down and removes the equipment. Keep the station familiar; do not add walking excitement and a heavier load together.
steps.advance: Brings the designated protected walk kit from its station and releases it without damaging equipment.
steps.easier: Keep the carrier empty or have the human collect equipment. Stop if weight, straps or chewing make the job unsuitable.

skills.title: Search a few open boxes
skills.goal: Find a safe food reward among a few open containers.
skills.setup: Wide shallow open boxes without staples or loose pieces, suitable food, and one dog at a time; supervise and skip for paper eaters.

steps.title: One obvious open box
steps.teach: Place a reward visibly in one shallow open box while the dog watches from nearby. Let them approach and eat it without needing a sit or nose hold. Repeat with easy placements and allow the dog to leave. The box is an invitation, not a barrier.
steps.advance: Comfortably approaches the box and finds the obvious food without chewing the container or climbing in.
steps.easier: Use a plate or floor scatter instead if boxes cause concern or chewing.

steps.title: Two separated containers
steps.teach: Arrange two familiar shallow boxes with space to walk around them. Let the dog watch you bait one, then invite a search. Reward discovery by letting them eat the food. Swap which box is baited and keep the task easy enough to avoid frantic digging.
steps.advance: Uses relaxed investigation to find the food in either familiar open box.
steps.easier: Reduce to one box or show the reward again. Remove unsafe or chewed materials immediately.

steps.title: A tiny hidden search
steps.teach: With the dog occupied comfortably nearby, place a small reward in one of three open boxes. Invite a search without pointing toward the right box. Keep containers open and accessible, and help by making the reward easier to notice before frustration develops.
steps.advance: Investigates the small array willingly and finds rewards with ordinary sniffing and comfortable movement.
steps.easier: Use fewer boxes, visible food, or plain ground search. Finding food is enrichment, not a clinical anxiety score.

skills.title: Unfold a loose food towel
skills.goal: Find food under one loose towel fold.
skills.setup: A clean flat towel, suitable food, and close supervision; skip if fabric is chewed, swallowed, or guarded.

steps.title: Food on the open towel
steps.teach: Lay a clean towel flat on a non-slip floor and place a few rewards on top where they are easy to see. Let the dog sniff and eat while you supervise. Remove the towel if chewing starts; no pulling, tying, or rolling is needed.
steps.advance: Eats the easy visible food with relaxed sniffing and no fabric chewing.
steps.easier: Use a suitable food mat or ordinary floor search instead.

steps.title: One very loose fold
steps.teach: Cover one reward with the towel’s edge, leaving part visible and a broad open route to reach it. Let the dog nudge the loose fold aside. Help promptly if it becomes frustrating. Keep the rest of the towel open and remove it when the game ends.
steps.advance: Comfortably finds rewards under one loose fold without grabbing or swallowing fabric.
steps.easier: Leave more food visible or keep the towel completely flat. Do not add knots or tight rolls.

skills.title: Find a partly hidden toy
skills.goal: Search for a safe familiar toy in easy nearby hiding places.
skills.setup: A safe favorite toy and an uncluttered room; no high shelves, tight spaces, or forced waits.

steps.title: Watch an easy placement
steps.teach: Let the dog see you place their familiar toy beside a clear floor marker. Invite them to find it and enjoy a short familiar play or give-and-reward game. Move the marker a little between attempts so the toy remains obvious and accessible.
steps.advance: Willingly locates the visible toy and enjoys the reward or play afterward.
steps.easier: Keep the toy at your feet or use ordinary fetch. Do not force a wait while hiding it.

steps.title: Hide only a small part
steps.teach: Place the toy partly behind a wide safe object with most of it still visible. Invite the search and remain neutral. When the dog finds it, reward with the play they enjoy. Increase concealment only a little and help before they give up or become frantic.
steps.advance: Investigates and finds several easy partly hidden placements with comfortable enthusiasm.
steps.easier: Show more of the toy or return to a visible placement. Avoid inaccessible or surprising hiding spots.

skills.title: Follow a short food trail
skills.goal: Follow a few easy spaced food rewards along a safe route.
skills.setup: A clean safe surface, suitable food and no other dogs competing; avoid unknown outdoor foods or unsafe ground.

steps.title: A visible short trail
steps.teach: Place a few suitable rewards a short paw-step apart on safe ground while the dog watches. Invite them to investigate the first and let them find the rest at their own pace. Walk alongside without steering their nose or pulling on equipment.
steps.advance: Follows the short visible line with comfortable sniffing and no frantic searching.
steps.easier: Use fewer rewards closer together, or choose an indoor floor search.

steps.title: One easy bend
steps.teach: Create a similarly short reward trail with one broad bend and a clearly accessible finish. Keep reward spacing easy and the route away from hazards. Let the dog choose the pace and stop when the small trail is finished; this is not a tracking test.
steps.advance: Enjoys following a short bent trail independently on a familiar safe surface.
steps.easier: Straighten or shorten the route. Food trails are enrichment, not proof of scent-tracking expertise.

skills.title: Find a familiar person
skills.goal: Locate one trusted person who is only slightly out of view.
skills.setup: Two familiar cooperative adults, clear exits and a dog comfortable with brief visual separation; skip for separation distress.

steps.title: Find the visible helper
steps.teach: Have the familiar helper stand a few steps away, quietly invite the dog over once, and reward the approach. Begin with both people visible. Let the dog move voluntarily; this is a cheerful person-finding game, not a restraint-and-release recall drill.
steps.advance: Comfortably approaches the visible helper and enjoys their reward or play.
steps.easier: Keep the people closer. Stop if leaving either person causes worry.

steps.title: A tiny partly hidden position
steps.teach: Let the dog see the helper step partly behind a wide doorway while remaining mostly visible. Say “find them” and let the helper make one gentle invitation if needed. Reward finding them. Reset with everyone together before trying again.
steps.advance: Willingly finds the partly visible helper without distress or frantic searching.
steps.easier: Keep the helper fully visible and closer. Do not use hiding to test separation tolerance.

steps.title: One easy out-of-view spot
steps.teach: After comfortable partial hides, let the helper step just behind the same open doorway. Keep the route clear and the absence momentary. Invite finding them and help immediately with a gentle voice if needed. Reward, reunite, and end after a few enjoyable turns.
steps.advance: Finds the nearby familiar helper with comfortable searching and quick ordinary recovery.
steps.easier: Return to partial visibility or skip. No closed doors, unfamiliar people, or prolonged hidden waits.

skills.title: Find and deliver a named toy
skills.goal: Combine familiar toy labels with a short search and gentle return.
skills.cue: Your familiar toy labels, then Find
skills.setup: Two safe named toys, easy accessible floor-level placements and a dog comfortable with this small search. No forced waits or separation tests.

steps.title: Choose and deliver
steps.teach: Put both familiar named toys nearby in full view. With neutral hands and gaze, request one label, receive the known give and reward. Swap toy positions and request each in mixed order. Build the label-to-delivery connection before hiding either object.
steps.advance: Chooses either requested toy and delivers comfortably with positions exchanged in two brief sessions.
steps.easier: Use one toy again or revisit mixed-position label choices; avoid repeated guessing.

steps.title: Search for one toy
steps.teach: With just one toy present, let the dog watch a partly concealed placement beside a broad safe object. Invite the familiar search and reward its return. Expose more of the toy whenever needed, then try a moment out of view only while searching stays comfortable.
steps.advance: Finds and returns either toy separately from several easy, partly concealed placements.
steps.easier: Use a visible floor placement or shorten the route. Skip separation that causes concern.

steps.title: Request a toy from two search spots
steps.teach: Place the two familiar toys in separate easy search spots. Begin with one fully visible, then partly conceal either one while keeping access open. Request each label across mixed placements and reward the requested delivery. Help before errors or frustration build.
steps.advance: Finds and delivers either named toy from both familiar search spots without pointing.
steps.easier: Expose both toys or return to a single-toy search.

steps.title: Transfer and finish
steps.teach: Have a familiar helper change one easy placement while you remain neutral beside the dog. Request a familiar toy, receive and reward its return, then give a clear finished cue. Keep new placements visible at first; a short successful search is enough.
steps.advance: Completes the small named search-and-return game with changed placements and comfortable finishing.
steps.easier: Keep the familiar placements and helpful component cues. This is not an intelligence test.

skills.title: Getting a drink from the fridge
skills.goal: Open an approved easy door, retrieve a protected drink carrier, deliver it, and finish with human or dog closure.
skills.cue: Fetch a drink (or your chosen word)
skills.setup: All components comfortable and consistent in this setting; fully supervised.

steps.title: Start with the easy ending
steps.teach: Rehearse an easy delivery from the open fridge with you one step away. Reward the give generously. On separate repetitions have the dog give a carrier already held near you. This keeps the final delivery fluent and rewarding before adding earlier links.
steps.advance: Easy deliveries remain reliable and enjoyable with gentle handling on 4 of 5 repetitions.
steps.easier: Shorten the carry and return to isolated give; do not add opening while delivery is uncertain.

steps.title: Add opening before pickup
steps.teach: Begin beside the approved fridge. Cue open, then the familiar pickup from its shelf, then give. Initially reward the opening component and the final delivery; over sessions reduce the intermediate food while continuing to cue and generously reward the complete easy chain.
steps.advance: Open → shelf pickup → delivery works gently with the familiar component cues on 4 of 5 attempts across two sessions.
steps.easier: Practice the broken link alone, then rejoin an easier two-link sequence. Avoid withholding all rewards to force a full chain.

steps.title: Add the optional return and close
steps.teach: For dog closure, first complete CLOSE-3; otherwise choose human closure and keep that as your final routine. After give, reward, then cue return → close and reward at the door. Rehearse this ending with a human-opened fridge before joining it to retrieval. Always check the seal yourself.
steps.advance: The chosen full sequence, with or without dog closure, is comfortable and reliable in two sessions.
steps.easier: Have a human close, or practice return/close separately. Keep your body clear of the dog’s path.

steps.title: Introduce one final request
steps.teach: Say the final request just before the familiar sequence, then provide component cues as needed. Across successful repetitions pause briefly before each extra cue so the next action can occur on its own. Fade one prompt at a time; reward completion and supervise. Remove rope and block access afterward.
steps.advance: Completes the chosen safe sequence on the final request with little or no extra prompting on 4 of 5 attempts in two sessions.
steps.easier: Restore the component cue at the difficult link, shorten starting distance, or omit closing. Keep contents protected and inspect the carrier each use.

project.parallel: Opening, shelf retrieval and gentle closing are separate skills. Practice their ready steps in any order. Rope pulling is required before door pulling; human closure is a complete, valid ending.

skills.title: Sort the toys
skills.goal: Recognize trained balls, stuffed toys and rope props, carry each to its matching basket and finish a mixed tidy-up.
skills.setup: Use the individually taught toy-to-basket assignments and three large marked baskets. All objects must suit this dog; reward correct deposits throughout. Do not assume untaught examples will generalize.

steps.title: Sort one of each
steps.teach: Place one familiar object for each destination on a clear floor, equally easy to reach. Invite a known pickup and matching deposit, reward, then invite another. Let the dog choose the order while you stay neutral about which destination is correct.
steps.advance: Sorts the three familiar objects into their respective baskets with comfortable, separately rewarded deposits.
steps.easier: Offer one object at a time and restore its known basket cue.

steps.title: Sort a mixed set
steps.teach: Add the separately taught second examples, starting with just one extra object. Mix where toys lie without also moving the marked baskets. Reward each correct deposit and reset to an easy pairing after an error; gradually offer all six familiar objects.
steps.advance: Sorts the six trained objects into three destinations with no repeated pattern of destination errors.
steps.easier: Use fewer objects or return to the isolated pairing that became uncertain.

steps.title: Follow the assignments after a layout change
steps.teach: Move each basket together with its own marker between rounds and shorten the toy-to-basket routes again. Keep your hands still after the invitation. Reward sorting by the practiced assignment rather than by old left, middle and right locations.
steps.advance: Sorts the trained objects after basket positions change, with little destination prompting.
steps.easier: Restore the familiar layout or use one object beside its destination.

steps.title: Complete a sorting round
steps.teach: Say the finished project cue once before the familiar tidy invitations. Pause for the next pickup when comfortable, supporting with component cues and rewards whenever needed. After the last deposit, give a clear finished cue and remove the setup rather than expecting endless searching.
steps.advance: Enjoys a mixed three-destination sorting round, chooses the practiced baskets and finishes comfortably on two occasions.
steps.easier: Keep individual pickup and basket cues. A successful three-object round is a valid smaller game.

project.parallel: Learn the first, second and third toy-to-basket pairings separately. Combine destination choices only when their component pairings are comfortable. New examples are taught, not presumed.

skills.title: Courier to a named person
skills.goal: Collect a protected message, identify the requested familiar adult, hand it to that person and return to the sender.
skills.cue: Take this to Sarah / Alex (your practiced names)
skills.setup: Two familiar willing recipients, safe pouch and tray, flat sender mat and clear indoor routes. Practice only taught names with visible recipients; no delivery of medication, valuables or loose ingestible items.

steps.title: Carry to the requested person
steps.teach: With both familiar recipients equally close and still, offer the familiar pouch and name the intended adult before the known delivery cue. Reward the correct handover, then invite the empty return. Request both people in mixed order, using no pointing or beckoning.
steps.advance: Gently delivers to either requested familiar adult and returns to the sender across position swaps.
steps.easier: Practice name choices without a pouch or deliver to one adult again.

steps.title: Keep the recipient choice through handover
steps.teach: Let the other adult remain visible while the intended receiver prepares their usual receiving hand only after the dog arrives. Reward the correct give and return. Vary who is nearer without offering competing treats, reaching for the pouch or correcting a wrong approach.
steps.advance: Maintains the named choice through handover even when the other familiar person is nearer.
steps.easier: Use equal distances or rehearse the harder name choice without an item.

steps.title: Collect the message before choosing
steps.teach: Begin at the tray with the familiar safe pouch containing one light protected note. Name the recipient, invite collection, then support the known chosen-person delivery and empty return. Reward at handover and at the sender’s mat; keep all people visible.
steps.advance: Connects tray pickup, named-recipient choice, give and empty return with familiar component cues.
steps.easier: Hand over the empty pouch at the start again or practice the uncertain component alone.

steps.title: Complete the named courier request
steps.teach: Give the chosen full request before the familiar round, pausing briefly before extra collection, delivery or return prompts. Alternate recipients and their easy positions over separate short turns. Reward both ends and finish after a round; never send the dog to find an absent or unfamiliar recipient.
steps.advance: Completes the named courier round for both practiced people across changed positions and distances with little prompting.
